q:
Consider the following statements about the extent of stock verification:
1. Items which are high in value or attractive in nature call for complete, cent per cent verification of the balances held.
2. For bulky and homogeneous stores held in large quantities, verification may be carried out in the manner prescribed for such stores, e.g. by weighment, measurement or sampling, instead of counting every single piece.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under the Indian Railway Stores Code, high-value and attractive items require cent per cent verification, while bulky homogeneous stores may be verified by weighment, measurement or sampling as prescribed. Hence both statements are correct.

q: The cash imprest held by a depot official for petty stores and depot expenses is produced for verification. The official accounts for the imprest correctly by producing:

options.A: Cash and duly supported vouchers for the expenditure incurred, which together equal the amount of the imprest held by him
options.B: Only the bin cards of the stores purchased from the imprest
options.C: A certificate from the supplier from whom stores were last purchased
options.D: The priced stores ledger folio of the items purchased

e: An imprest holder must account for the full imprest by cash in hand plus duly supported vouchers for expenditure incurred, the two together equalling the imprest amount, as required for imprest accountal under the Stores Code.

q: During verification, the physical quantity of an item tallies exactly with the book quantity, but the value of the stock differs because the book rate applied in the priced ledger is not the current average rate of the item. This difference is in the nature of a:

options.A: Price (value) difference, to be adjusted in the priced accounts through the Stock Adjustment Account without altering any quantity record
options.B: Quantity difference, to be recorded on a stock sheet as a shortage
options.C: Loss by theft, to be reported to the police
options.D: Sales difference, to be credited to Sales Suspense

e: Where quantity tallies but value differs due to a wrong book rate, it is a price difference only. It is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account in the priced accounts without any quantity entry on a stock sheet.

q:
Consider the following statements about the causes of overstocking of stores in a depot:
1. Indenting for quantities in excess of requirements, without taking into account the stock already in hand and the dues already on order, leads to overstocking.
2. Curtailment or abandonment of the programme for which stores were procured can leave the depot overstocked with those stores.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Overstocking arises both from indenting in excess of requirements without reckoning stock in hand and dues on order, and from curtailment or abandonment of the programme for which stores were procured, as recognised in Stores Code inventory control provisions.

q: The inventory turnover of the stores of a railway, as distinct from its Turnover Ratio, expresses:

options.A: The closing balance of stores as a proportion of the total issues
options.B: The value of scrap sold during the year as a proportion of the stock held
options.C: The earnest money collected as a proportion of the purchases made
options.D: How many times the average stock held is issued and replenished during the year, a higher turnover indicating that stock is moving faster in relation to the capital locked up in it

e: Inventory turnover shows how many times average stock is issued and replenished in a year. A higher turnover means stock moves faster and less capital remains locked up, unlike the Turnover Ratio which relates closing balance to issues.

q: The total lead time after which a demanded stock item actually becomes available for issue in the depot comprises:

options.A: Only the time taken by the supplier to despatch the material
options.B: The administrative time in processing the demand, vetting and placing the order, the supplier's delivery time, and the time taken in transit, inspection and acceptance into stock
options.C: Only the time taken in inspection of the material at destination
options.D: Only the time between two successive stock verifications

e: Total lead time under the Stores Code covers administrative processing and ordering time, supplier delivery time, and transit, inspection and acceptance time, until the item is actually available for issue in the depot.

q: At a periodical review, the recorded consumption of an item shows a sustained change over a period, while the stock limits of the item were fixed on the old pattern of consumption. The correct action is that:

options.A: The stock limits are revised in the light of the sustained consumption data, so that the maximum, minimum and re-order levels correspond to the actual requirements
options.B: The limits are never revised, having once been fixed
options.C: The item is deleted from the Priced Vocabulary at once
options.D: Fresh stock is ordered up to the old maximum level in all cases, ignoring the consumption data

e: Stock limits - maximum, minimum and re-order levels - are fixed from consumption and must be revised when recorded consumption shows a sustained change, so that limits reflect actual requirements.

q: A new stores item, a type of pump allied to the pumps already stocked by the depots, is introduced for stocking. Under the codification system, the item is correctly allotted:

options.A: A PL number in an entirely unconnected group, so that it is not confused with the existing pumps
options.B: The same PL number as an existing pump of a different description
options.C: A distinct PL number within the group of allied items to which pumps belong, so that the item is identified with its group and yet distinguished from every other item
options.D: No PL number, pumps being non-stock items in all cases

e: Under PL codification in the Priced Vocabulary, allied items are grouped together. A new pump allied to existing pumps gets a distinct PL number within the pumps group, preserving group identity while distinguishing the item.

q: Unification of specifications of stores across the Railways means that:

options.A: Every depot frames its own specification for the same item
options.B: Only one supplier is permitted to supply the item to all railways
options.C: Specifications are dispensed with and stores are bought by brand name only
options.D: The same item is procured to a common, unified specification on all railways, so that the item is interchangeable and can be transferred and used across railways

e: Unification means the same item is procured to a common unified specification on all railways. The item is therefore interchangeable and can be transferred and used across railways.

q:
Consider the following statements about standardisation of stores, which reduces a large number of slightly differing varieties of fasteners to a smaller number of standard sizes:
1. Inventory is reduced and procurement is simplified, as larger quantities of fewer standard items are bought.
2. Standard items can be interchanged in use more readily than a large number of slightly differing varieties.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Standardisation to fewer standard sizes reduces inventory and simplifies procurement through larger buys of fewer items, and standard items are more readily interchangeable in use than many slightly differing varieties.

q: After a purchase order has been placed, the consignee depot named in the order is changed because the depot originally named has been closed. This change is correctly given effect to by:

options.A: A formal amendment to the purchase order issued by the purchase office, with copies to the supplier, the old and new consignees and the Accounts office
options.B: A verbal intimation by the depot storekeeper to the supplier
options.C: Cancelling the tender itself and inviting fresh offers
options.D: Altering the receipt note after the material has been received elsewhere

e: A change of consignee after placement of a purchase order can be effected only by a formal amendment issued by the purchase office, with copies to the supplier, old and new consignees and Accounts, as required under the IRS Conditions of Contract procedure.

q: A purchase order provides for supply of the ordered quantity in staggered lots over a period. Within the overall delivery period of the contract, the supplier seeks a change in the dates of the individual lots. Such rescheduling of the delivery schedule is dealt with by:

options.A: The stock verifier, by amending the stock sheet
options.B: Treating every such request as a fresh tender
options.C: The supplier himself, without informing the Railway
options.D: The competent purchase authority, which may approve the revised schedule by an amendment to the order where the overall contract delivery obligation is not prejudiced

e: Rescheduling of staggered deliveries within the overall delivery period is decided by the competent purchase authority by amendment to the order, provided the overall contract delivery obligation is not prejudiced.

q: Stores offered for pre-despatch inspection are rejected, rectified by the supplier and offered again for inspection. The charges of the re-inspection, occasioned by the supplier's initial failure, are:

options.A: Borne by the consignee depot in all cases
options.B: Adjusted through the Sales Suspense Account
options.C: Recoverable from the supplier, the re-inspection having become necessary due to the stores first offered not conforming to the specification
options.D: Paid out of the earnest money of the other tenderers

e: Re-inspection charges occasioned by the supplier offering non-conforming stores in the first instance are recoverable from the supplier under the IRS Conditions of Contract, the re-inspection being necessitated by his failure.

q: Bulk supplies of an item are received against a purchase order which was placed on the basis of an approved sample. On inspection, the bulk supply is found to differ materially from the approved sample, though the supplier claims it serves the same purpose. The bulk supply is correctly:

options.A: Accepted at the full contract rate by the storekeeper, the purpose being served
options.B: Issued to the user department with a note of the difference
options.C: Not accepted as conforming supply, the bulk being required to conform to the approved sample, and dealt with under the contract by rejection or by acceptance under a deviation with price reduction by the competent authority
options.D: Taken into stock as a new item under a fresh PL number

e: Bulk supply against an approved sample must conform to that sample. Material differing materially is not conforming supply and is liable to rejection, or acceptance only under deviation with price reduction by the competent authority.

q: A latent defect in stores supplied against a contract is noticed during use, well within the warranty period, and a warranty claim is lodged on the supplier promptly with full particulars of the defect. The supplier objects that the stores have already been put to use. The correct position is that:

options.A: Use of the stores automatically extinguishes the warranty, whatever the defect
options.B: The claim is in order if the defect is covered by the warranty and the claim is lodged within the warranty period; the supplier is required to repair or replace the defective stores under the warranty clause
options.C: The claim can be lodged only by the stock verifier
options.D: The defective stores must first be sold as scrap before any claim can be made

e: Under the warranty clause of the IRS Conditions of Contract, a latent defect claim lodged within the warranty period with full particulars is valid even if stores were put to use, and the supplier must repair or replace the defective stores.

q: A supplier whose supplies were delayed for reasons attributable to him requests that the liquidated damages leviable under the contract be waived altogether. The waiver can be granted only:

options.A: By the depot storekeeper who received the stores
options.B: By the supplier himself by a letter to the depot
options.C: Automatically, on the expiry of the warranty period
options.D: By the competent authority empowered to do so, for reasons to be recorded, liquidated damages being otherwise recoverable under the contract

e: Liquidated damages leviable for delay are recoverable under the contract and can be waived only by the competent authority empowered to do so, for reasons recorded, not by the depot storekeeper or the supplier.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An extension of the delivery period may be considered along with a reduction in the contract price where the market price of the item has fallen, so that the Railway is not made to pay the old higher rate for the delayed supplies.
2. A price reduction under such an arrangement is imposed by the depot storekeeper without reference to the contract or the competent authority.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: An extension of delivery period may be considered with a price reduction where market prices have fallen, so the Railway does not pay the old higher rate for delayed supplies. Such reduction is imposed only by the competent authority under the contract, not by the storekeeper alone. Hence statement 1 only is correct.

q: Goods supplied against an order placed on the Government e-Marketplace are received at the consignee depot and are found, on inspection, not to conform to the order. The consignee correctly records the outcome by:

options.A: Generating the Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate for the full quantity as if the goods had been accepted
options.B: Taking the goods into priced stock and raising a stock sheet for the difference
options.C: Paying the seller in cash from the depot imprest
options.D: Not generating acceptance for the rejected goods on the portal, and recording the rejection/non-acceptance through the portal procedure so that payment is not released for the rejected supply

e: On GeM, acceptance is recorded through the portal. Rejected non-conforming goods must not be covered by acceptance or CRAC, and rejection is recorded through the portal so payment is not released for the rejected supply.

q:
Consider the following statements about the estimated quantity shown in a rate contract:
1. The estimate is indicative of the expected requirement, and supplies are ordered as and when required during the currency of the contract.
2. A variation between the estimated quantity and the quantity actually ordered does not by itself give the supplier a claim, the estimate not being a firm commitment to order that quantity.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In a rate contract the estimated quantity is only indicative of expected requirement, supplies being ordered as required during currency. Variation from the estimate alone gives no claim, as the estimate is not a firm commitment to order that quantity.

q: In a grave emergency, stores are procured and put to use at once to restore train services, the normal sanction procedure not having been completed beforehand. The transaction is regularised by:

options.A: Omitting the purchase from the accounts altogether, the emergency being sufficient justification
options.B: Bringing the facts on record promptly, with the urgency justification, and obtaining the post-facto sanction of the competent authority for the procurement
options.C: Showing the stores as received free of cost from the supplier
options.D: Debiting the cost to the personal account of the depot storekeeper

e: Emergency procurement to restore services must be brought on record promptly with urgency justification and regularised by post-facto sanction of the competent authority; it cannot be omitted from accounts.

q: In the periodical review of stores suspense balances, the outstanding items under Purchase Suspense and Stores Miscellaneous Suspense are examined age-wise mainly in order to:

options.A: Increase the closing balance of stores of the railway
options.B: Identify the old and long-outstanding debits and credits, pursue their linking, recovery or adjustment, and prevent suspense balances from accumulating uncleared
options.C: Fix the reserve price of scrap lots awaiting auction
options.D: Revise the book rates of all stock items

e: Age-wise review of Purchase Suspense and Stores Miscellaneous Suspense under the Stores Code identifies old outstanding debits and credits for linking, recovery or adjustment, preventing accumulation of uncleared suspense balances.

q: Material has been received and taken into stock at a depot, but the receipt remains unlinked in the accounts because the supplier's bill and the corresponding purchase order particulars have not been matched with it. Until the linking is completed, the receipt:

options.A: Is written off through the Stock Adjustment Account as a loss
options.B: Is removed from the priced stores ledger at the end of the month
options.C: Is treated as a sale to the supplier
options.D: Remains outstanding in the suspense/accounts records as an unlinked receipt, to be pursued by the depot and the Accounts office until it is linked with the bill and the order and finally adjusted

e: A receipt not yet linked with the supplier bill and purchase order particulars remains an unlinked receipt outstanding in suspense and accounts records, to be pursued by depot and Accounts until linked and finally adjusted.

q: A field official makes a petty emergency purchase of stores locally out of his cash imprest. The purchase is accounted for by:

options.A: Retaining the material without any voucher or entry
options.B: Rendering an account supported by the cash memo/vouchers for the purchase, so that the expenditure is adjusted in the accounts and the imprest is recouped to that extent
options.C: Debiting the amount to Sales Suspense permanently
options.D: Recovering the amount from the depot storekeeper's pay

e: A petty emergency purchase from cash imprest is accounted for by rendering cash memos and vouchers for the purchase, so expenditure is adjusted and the imprest recouped to that extent.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Daily Receipt Register of a stores depot:
1. All material received at the depot, from whatever source, is in the first instance entered in the register at the time it is received, before its inspection, binning and posting in the bin card and priced accounts.
2. Entry in the Daily Receipt Register by itself treats the material as accepted into priced stock, without any inspection.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Daily Receipt Register records all material received in the first instance at the time of receipt, before inspection and binning. Entry therein alone does not constitute acceptance into priced stock, which follows only after inspection and receipt note. Hence statement 1 only is correct.

q: The Priced Vocabulary of stores and its PL codification are unified in their application, so that the same item bears the same PL number wherever it is stocked. This unification principally helps in that:

options.A: Each depot can change the description of the item to suit local practice
options.B: Stock of the same item held in other depots and railways can be located and compared, e.g. through iMMS, and transfers can be arranged against a common identification of the item
options.C: The book rate of the item becomes the same for every purchase from every supplier
options.D: Stock verification of the item is no longer necessary in any depot

e: Unified Priced Vocabulary and PL codification give the same item the same PL number everywhere, enabling stock in other depots and railways to be located and compared, for example through iMMS, and transfers arranged on common identification.

q: Stores despatched by a supplier arrive at the consignee depot, but their acceptance into stock is held up because the prescribed inspection at destination is delayed. For the consuming department, the effect is correctly described as that:

options.A: The transit time alone determines the availability of the stores
options.B: The inspection and acceptance time at destination also forms part of the total time before the stores become available for issue, and is therefore a component of the effective lead time
options.C: Inspection time is counted as consumption time of the item
options.D: The stores are deemed to be in stock from the date of despatch for all purposes

e: Inspection and acceptance time at destination is part of the total time before stores become available for issue, and is therefore a component of effective lead time, not merely transit time.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Liquidated damages under a stores contract relate to delay in supply, while the warranty clause relates to defects in the stores supplied; the two operate independently of each other.
2. Levy of liquidated damages for delayed supply extinguishes the supplier's liability under the warranty clause for the same supply.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Liquidated damages relate to delay in supply while warranty relates to defects; they operate independently under the IRS Conditions of Contract. Levy of liquidated damages does not extinguish warranty liability. Hence statement 1 only is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about a common-use stores item covered by a rate contract arrangement on the Government e-Marketplace:
1. The requirement is met by placing the order through the GeM portal against the arrangement available thereon, the supply and payment being processed through the portal.
2. The requirement may instead be met by a verbal order on the firm outside the portal, with payment in cash from the depot.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A common-use item covered by a GeM rate arrangement must be ordered through the GeM portal with supply and payment processed thereon. A verbal order outside the portal with cash payment from depot imprest is not permissible. Hence statement 1 only is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Standardisation reduces the number of varieties of an item stocked within the railway by adopting standard specifications and sizes.
2. Unification carries the process further by adopting common specifications and codification for the item across railways, so that the same item is identified and procured uniformly everywhere.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Standardisation reduces varieties within a railway by adopting standard specifications and sizes, while unification adopts common specifications and codification across railways for uniform identification and procurement everywhere. Hence both statements are correct.

q: During a month, several lots of scrap sold earlier are delivered to the purchasers and the depot renders the monthly sale account to the Accounts office. On the basis of that account, the Accounts office:

options.A: Credits the entire sale value again to Purchase Suspense
options.B: Finally adjusts the sale value held under Sales Suspense for the lots delivered to the appropriate heads, the book value of the lots being relieved from the stock accounts
options.C: Places purchase orders for fresh stores equal to the quantity sold
options.D: Revises the AAC of the items sold as scrap

e: On the monthly sale account, Accounts finally adjusts sale value held under Sales Suspense for lots actually delivered to the appropriate heads, relieving the book value of the lots from stock accounts.

q: For an import of stores, the Railway arranges payment to the foreign supplier through a Letter of Credit. A Letter of Credit is:

options.A: A letter issued by the Railway Board to the foreign supplier assuring him of payment
options.B: A form prescribed by the Customs Department for assessment of duty on the consignment
options.C: An inspection certificate issued by the inspecting authority abroad
options.D: An undertaking of a bank to pay the foreign supplier against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents

e: A Letter of Credit is a bank undertaking to pay the foreign supplier against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents, and is the normal payment mechanism for imported stores.

q:
Consider the following statements about payment under a Letter of Credit opened for imported stores:
1. Payment to the foreign supplier is made against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents through the bank, and not on the physical receipt of the material in India.
2. Payment under a Letter of Credit is made only after the material has been received and verified in the Indian depot.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Payment under a Letter of Credit is made against presentation of stipulated shipping documents through the bank, not on physical receipt in India. Hence statement 1 only is correct; statement 2, requiring prior receipt and verification in the depot, is wrong.

q: An imported item reaches a depot and the Accounts office has to book its stock value. The supplier's invoice shows only the purchase price, but the value at which the item is taken into stock must also take into account:

options.A: Nothing beyond the purchase price shown in the invoice
options.B: Only the freight paid for bringing the item to the depot
options.C: Freight, insurance and customs duty, in addition to the purchase price, making up the landed cost
options.D: The purchase price reduced by the customs duty paid

e: Imported stores are taken into stock at landed cost, comprising purchase price plus freight, insurance and customs duty, as prescribed for valuation of imported stores in the Stores Code.

q:
Consider the following statements about import terms for stores:
1. On CIF terms, the price quoted by the foreign supplier includes cost, insurance and freight up to the port of destination.
2. On FOB terms, the price covers cost, insurance and freight up to the destination port in India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: On CIF terms price includes cost, insurance and freight to the destination port. On FOB terms price is free on board at the shipment port and does not include insurance and freight to India. Hence statement 1 only is correct.

q: Customs duty on a consignment of imported stores is payable:

options.A: Before the consignment is cleared through Customs at the port of entry
options.B: By the foreign supplier in all cases, the Railway paying nothing
options.C: Only if the stores are later sold as scrap
options.D: Only after the close of the financial year of import

e: Customs duty must be paid before the consignment is cleared through Customs at the port of entry; clearance and onward movement follow only after duty payment.

q: Before a high-value stores tender is decided, the purchaser and all bidders sign a document committing both sides to refrain from corrupt practices, and Independent External Monitors oversee compliance with it. This document is the:

options.A: Security deposit bond furnished by the successful tenderer
options.B: Liquidated damages clause of the contract
options.C: Integrity Pact
options.D: Fall clause of the purchase order

e: The document committing purchaser and bidders to refrain from corrupt practices, overseen by Independent External Monitors in high-value tenders, is the Integrity Pact.

q: In a stores tender, the lowest offer is from a firm of a country which shares a land border with India, but the firm produces no registration with the Registration Committee set up by the DPIIT. Under Rule 144(xi) of the General Financial Rules, the offer:

options.A: Must be accepted, registration being a mere formality
options.B: Cannot make the firm eligible to participate, such registration being a condition of eligibility
options.C: Can be accepted with the approval of the depot officer inviting the tender
options.D: Can be accepted if the firm is exempted from earnest money

e: Under GFR Rule 144(xi), a bidder from a country sharing a land border with India is eligible only if registered with the Registration Committee set up by DPIIT. Without such registration the firm cannot be eligible, however low its offer.

q: To keep a stores purchase within his own financial powers, an officer splits a single demand into several smaller indents. Such splitting of a demand or indent merely to bring it within the financial powers of a lower authority is:

options.A: A recommended measure of economy
options.B: Permitted at the level of the depot officer
options.C: Permitted with the approval of the storekeeper
options.D: Not permissible

e: Splitting a single demand into smaller indents merely to keep the purchase within the financial powers of a lower authority is prohibited under GFR and Stores Code financial propriety rules; it is not permissible at any depot level.

q: A railway workshop manufactures an item and transfers it to a stores depot for stocking. The item is taken into stock at:

options.A: The prevailing market price of similar material
options.B: The cost of manufacture, comprising material, labour and on-cost, as worked out through the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: The cost of the raw material alone
options.D: A nominal value of one rupee per unit

e: Workshop-manufactured items transferred to a depot are taken into stock at cost of manufacture - material, labour and on-cost - worked out through the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, not at market price or raw material cost alone.

q: An external audit party takes up the audit of the stores accounts of a zonal railway. This audit is conducted on behalf of:

options.A: The chartered accountants engaged by the suppliers
options.B: The depot storekeeper, as an internal arrangement
options.C: The Stores Tender Committee of the railway
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India, through the Railway Audit organisation

e: External audit of stores accounts is statutory audit conducted on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India through the Railway Audit organisation, distinct from internal check.

q: A micro enterprise supplied stores to a depot, but its bill remains unpaid well beyond the date agreed for payment. Apart from the principal amount of the bill, the Railway must also bear, under the MSMED Act:

options.A: No further amount of any kind
options.B: Interest on the delayed payment, as provided in the Act
options.C: A penalty equal to the amount of the bill
options.D: The departmental charges on the supply

e: Under the MSMED Act, delayed payment to a micro or small enterprise beyond the agreed or appointed date attracts interest on the delayed payment as provided in the Act, in addition to the principal bill amount.

q: GST is paid on a stores purchase and input tax credit of the GST is available to the Railway. In the priced accounts, the GST amount is:

options.A: Not added to the cost of the stores, the credit being accounted for separately
options.B: Added in full to the book value of the stores in the Priced Stores Ledger
options.C: Recovered from the depot storekeeper
options.D: Treated as part of the inventory carrying cost of the item

e: Where GST input tax credit is available, GST is not added to the cost of stores in the priced accounts; the credit is accounted for separately, so book value excludes the creditable GST.

q: A depot despatches stores to a depot of another zonal railway and the receiving railway asks how the value will be settled, there being no cash payment between the railways. The settlement is effected:

options.A: Without any document, on the basis of a telephone message
options.B: By treating the material as sold in the open market
options.C: In one lump sum at the close of the financial year
options.D: Through the inter-railway transfer/adjustment accounts, on the basis of priced transfer notes

e: Inter-railway transfers are settled without cash through inter-railway transfer and adjustment accounts on the basis of priced transfer notes issued for the material despatched.

q: Equipment ordered by the Railways is under manufacture at the supplier's works, and inspection is carried out in stages during the process of manufacture itself. Such inspection is known as:

options.A: Stage inspection
options.B: Surprise inspection
options.C: Post-delivery inspection
options.D: Stock verification

e: Inspection carried out in stages during manufacture at the supplier works is stage inspection, distinct from post-delivery inspection, surprise inspection or stock verification.

q: A depot custodian offers to draw up the programme for the periodical verification of his own depot, so that verification suits his convenience. The programme of periodical stock verification is actually drawn up by:

options.A: The custodian of the depot himself
options.B: The suppliers of the stores held in the depot
options.C: The Stores Tender Committee
options.D: The Accounts Department

e: The programme of periodical stock verification is drawn up by the Accounts Department, not by the depot custodian, to ensure independent verification under the Stores Code.

q: A depot storekeeper, finding an item in excess of his depot's requirements, proposes to declare it surplus on his own authority and offer it for disposal. The correct position is that stores are formally declared surplus:

options.A: By the depot storekeeper on his own authority
options.B: By the competent authority, after review of the stock position and circulation of the items to other depots and railways
options.C: By the stock verifier who verified the item
options.D: By the purchaser who offers to buy the item

e: Stores are declared surplus only by the competent authority after review of stock position and circulation to other depots and railways; a depot storekeeper cannot declare surplus or offer disposal on his own authority.

q: When material against a purchase order arrives, the consignee depot checks it against its copy of the order, and the Accounts office later checks the supplier's bill against its own copy. The copies are distributed to the depot and the Accounts office primarily for this purpose of:

options.A: Advertising the order in newspapers
options.B: Evaluating the tenders received against the order
options.C: Linking the material received and the supplier's bill with the purchase order
options.D: Fixing the AAC of the item ordered

e: Copies of the purchase order are distributed to the consignee depot and Accounts primarily for linking - the depot links material received and Accounts links the supplier bill with the purchase order.

q: A truck carrying stores sold from a depot is stopped at the depot gate and the driver can produce no document authorising the removal. Stores or scrap can be taken out of a stores depot only against:

options.A: A verbal permission given by any depot official
options.B: A copy of the tender notice for the item
options.C: The bin card maintained at the bin
options.D: A gate pass issued on the basis of the issue note or delivery order, as the case may be

e: No stores or scrap can be removed from a depot without a gate pass issued on the basis of the issue note or delivery order; a verbal permission, tender notice or bin card does not authorise removal.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Priced Stores Ledger of a depot is maintained by the Stores Accounts office of the Accounts Department.
2. The Bin Cards of a depot, recording quantities only, are maintained by the storekeeper at the bins.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Priced Stores Ledger, with quantity and value, is maintained by the Stores Accounts office of Accounts, while Bin Cards recording quantities only are maintained by the storekeeper at the bins. Hence both statements are correct.

q: A note describes materials management as consisting of purchasing alone. That description is incomplete, because materials management on the Railways embraces:

options.A: Purchasing, and nothing beyond it
options.B: Custody and storage of stores, and nothing beyond them
options.C: Forecasting, procurement, stocking, inventory control and disposal of stores
options.D: Disposal of scrap and surplus stores, and nothing beyond it

e: Materials management on the Railways embraces forecasting, procurement, stocking, inventory control and disposal of stores as a whole; describing it as purchasing alone is incomplete.

q: The Principal Chief Materials Manager heading the stores organisation of a zonal railway is an officer of the:

options.A: Indian Railway Accounts Service
options.B: Indian Railway Traffic Service
options.C: Indian Railway Personnel Service
options.D: Indian Railway Stores Service

e: The Principal Chief Materials Manager heads the stores organisation of a zonal railway and is an officer of the Indian Railway Stores Service, not Accounts, Traffic or Personnel.

q: In a stores tender, one firm quotes the lowest ex-works price, but its freight and taxes to destination are the highest. For comparison of the offers, the rates are compared on the basis of:

options.A: The ex-works price quoted by the tenderers only
options.B: The total price payable by the Railway at destination, including freight, taxes and duties
options.C: The price quoted by the tenderer recommended by the executive
options.D: The last accepted rate for the item

e: Offers are compared on the total price payable at destination, including freight, taxes and duties, not on ex-works price alone, so the lowest landed cost to the Railway is identified.

q: A supplier asks the depot to give him, in writing, the formal intimation that his stores have been refused on inspection so that he can arrange their removal. The document issued to him for this purpose is the:

options.A: Rejection Note
options.B: Receipt Note
options.C: Bin Card
options.D: Stock Sheet

e: The formal intimation to a supplier that his stores have been refused on inspection, to enable removal, is the Rejection Note, distinct from a Receipt Note, Bin Card or Stock Sheet.

q:
Consider the following statements about registration of firms for supply of stores:
1. Registration is granted for specific items or groups of items, and not generally for all stores items.
2. Registration is granted after assessing the firm's capacity-cum-capability and financial status.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Registration of firms is granted for specific items or groups after assessing capacity-cum-capability and financial status; it is not a general registration for all stores. Hence both statements are correct.

q: A sample of oil received in a depot is required to be tested before the bulk supply is accepted. Where testing is prescribed, such samples of oils, paints, chemicals and metals are tested in:

options.A: The supplier's own laboratory only
options.B: The depot storekeeper's office
options.C: The office of the Tender Committee
options.D: The Chemical and Metallurgical laboratory of the railway

e: Samples of oils, paints, chemicals and metals requiring test before acceptance are tested in the Chemical and Metallurgical laboratory of the railway, not in the supplier laboratory or depot office.

q: A stores officer proposes to accept a tender of a value beyond the limit up to which he is empowered, claiming discretion in the matter. The limits up to which stores officers may accept tenders and sanction purchases are actually laid down in:

options.A: The personal discretion of the officer concerned
options.B: The Indian Railways Act, 1989
options.C: The supplier's terms of offer
options.D: The delegation of powers under the Model Schedule of Powers (SOP)

e: Limits for acceptance of tenders and sanction of purchases by stores officers are laid down in the delegation of powers under the Model Schedule of Powers, not in personal discretion or the supplier terms.

q: A firm which missed a stores tender notice on IREPS asks where else railway stores tenders are published, so that it can watch that source as well. Apart from IREPS, the tenders are published on the:

options.A: Central Public Procurement (CPP) Portal
options.B: GeM portal only
options.C: Website of the lowest tenderer
options.D: Notice board of the depot only

e: Apart from publication on IREPS, railway stores tenders are published on the Central Public Procurement Portal, as required for public procurement transparency.

q: A supplier points out that a special condition printed in his purchase order conflicts with a provision of the IRS Conditions of Contract and asks which one governs the contract. The correct position is that:

options.A: The IRS Conditions of Contract prevail and the special condition is void
options.B: The special condition incorporated in the purchase order prevails over the general (IRS) conditions
options.C: The purchase order itself becomes void
options.D: The matter must be referred to the Railway Board in every such case

e: A special condition incorporated in the purchase order prevails over the general IRS Conditions of Contract to the extent of conflict, the special condition being the parties agreed term for that contract.

q: Goods ordered on the Government e-Marketplace are received at the consignee depot and accepted. On GeM, payment to the seller is processed after the consignee generates the:

options.A: Purchase Suspense statement
options.B: Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate (CRAC)
options.C: Stock sheet
options.D: Letter of Acceptance

e: On GeM, payment to the seller is processed only after the consignee generates the Consignee Receipt and Acceptance Certificate (CRAC) confirming receipt and acceptance of the goods.

q:
Consider the following statements about insurance of railway stores:
1. Railway stores held in depots are ordinarily insured with a commercial insurer against fire and theft.
2. Government follows the principle of bearing its own risks and does not ordinarily insure its own property.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Government follows the principle of self-insurance and bears its own risks, so railway stores in depots are not ordinarily insured commercially against fire and theft. Hence statement 2 only is correct.

q: A firm tries to submit its bid for a stores tender on IREPS but the system will not accept the submission. A bid on IREPS can be submitted only by a firm which has:

options.A: A seller registration on the GeM portal only
options.B: A valid Digital Signature Certificate
options.C: A bank guarantee from a nationalised bank
options.D: An ISO certification for its products

e: Submission of a bid on IREPS requires a valid Digital Signature Certificate for authentication and non-repudiation; GeM registration, bank guarantee or ISO certification alone does not enable IREPS submission.

q: A stock verifier reaches a depot to verify the stock, but the custodian is away on duty and has left no representative. Verification in such a situation is required to be carried out:

options.A: In the presence of the stockholder (custodian) or his authorised representative
options.B: From the bin cards alone, without opening the bins
options.C: In the absence of all depot staff
options.D: Only for the items selected by the stockholder

e: Stock verification must be carried out in the presence of the stockholder or his authorised representative, so the custodian can witness counts and explain differences on the spot.

q:
Consider the following statements about disputes under a stores contract:
1. Disputes between the Railway and a supplier which cannot be settled mutually are referred to arbitration under the IRS Conditions of Contract.
2. The arbitrator for such disputes is appointed by the General Manager of the Railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under the IRS Conditions of Contract, unresolved disputes are referred to arbitration, with the arbitrator appointed by the General Manager of the Railway. Hence both statements are correct.

q: A depot begins stocking a newly introduced item for which no consumption figures of past years exist. In the absence of past consumption, the AAC of the item is fixed on the basis of:

options.A: The anticipated requirement of the item assessed by the user department
options.B: The AAC of a similar item stocked on another railway
options.C: The maximum stock level prescribed for the depot
options.D: The quantity covered by the first purchase order placed for the item

e: For a newly stocked item with no past consumption, AAC is fixed on the anticipated requirement assessed by the user department, which forms the initial basis until actual consumption data becomes available.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The stock verifiers who carry out the physical verification of stores in depots function under the Accounts Department, in the FA&CAO's organisation.
2. The stock verifiers function under the Stores Department, headed by the Principal Chief Materials Manager.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Stock verifiers function under the Accounts Department in the FA and CAO organisation, ensuring independence from the Stores Department headed by the PCMM. Hence statement 1 only is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts:
1. Any disagreement between the priced ledger balances and the balances in the general books is investigated and reconciled.
2. The Balance Sheet covers only the priced stock balances, the stores suspense balances being left out of it.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In the Stores Balance Sheet any disagreement between priced ledger balances and general books balances is investigated and reconciled, and the Balance Sheet covers suspense balances as well as priced stock. Hence statement 1 only is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about departmental charges on stores transactions:
1. Departmental charges are added to the book rate when stores are transferred from one depot to another depot of the same railway.
2. Departmental charges are added to the book rate when stores are issued to outside parties and other Government departments.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Departmental charges are not added on transfers between depots of the same railway, but are added when stores are issued to outside parties and other Government departments. Hence statement 2 only is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about samples in stores procurement:
1. Where the tender conditions so stipulate, tenderers submit samples with their offers so that the quality and conformity of the stores offered can be judged while evaluating the tenders.
2. Where purchase is made on the basis of an approved sample, the sample is sealed and retained so that the bulk supplies can be compared with it at the time of inspection.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Samples stipulated in tender conditions are submitted with offers to judge quality at evaluation, and where purchase is on an approved sample it is sealed and retained for comparison with bulk supplies at inspection. Hence both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Safety (buffer) stock does not enter the Economic Order Quantity computation, but is taken into account in fixing the re-order level so that the buffer is available during the lead time.
2. Safety (buffer) stock is ordered afresh along with every order placed for the item.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Safety stock is not part of the EOQ computation, which covers ordering and carrying costs of the cycle stock, but is added in fixing the re-order level to provide buffer cover during lead time. It is not re-ordered afresh with every order. Hence statement 1 only is correct.

q: HML analysis of inventory is distinguished from ABC analysis in that HML classifies items on the basis of:

options.A: Their annual consumption value
options.B: Their criticality in use
options.C: Their unit price — High, Medium and Low
options.D: Their rate of movement from the depot

e: HML analysis classifies items by unit price into High, Medium and Low, unlike ABC which uses annual consumption value, VED which uses criticality, and FSN which uses movement rate.

q: An inventory review groups items as Government, Ordinary, Local and Foreign, according to where each item is obtained from. This method of grouping items by their source of supply is:

options.A: ABC analysis
options.B: VED analysis
options.C: GOLF analysis
options.D: FSN analysis

e: GOLF analysis groups items by source of supply - Government, Ordinary, Local and Foreign - unlike ABC, VED and FSN which classify on value, criticality and movement respectively.

q: A depot reorganises its supplies of a regularly consumed item so that each consignment reaches it just as the item is needed for use, and the stock held at any time is negligible. The inventory approach being followed is:

options.A: Holding the maximum possible stock in the depot
options.B: Stocking for a full year's consumption at a time
options.C: The Just-in-Time (JIT) approach
options.D: Doubling the safety stock of the item

e: Receiving each consignment just as it is needed, with negligible stock held, is the Just-in-Time approach to inventory, opposite to maximum stocking or annual bulk stocking.

q: A depot holds large numbers of low-value fasteners and similar C-category items consumed in bulk. The two-bin system of inventory control, in which the reserve bin is opened only when the working bin is exhausted, is ordinarily applied to:

options.A: A-category high-value items
options.B: Imported items purchased against letters of credit
options.C: Insurance spares of important equipment
options.D: Low-value C-category items consumed in large numbers

e: The two-bin system, where the reserve bin is opened only on exhaustion of the working bin, is ordinarily applied to low-value C-category items consumed in large numbers, where elaborate control is uneconomical.

q: A railway carries heavy outstanding debit balances under Purchase Suspense for bills paid but material not received. The effect of such balances on the stores position is that they:

options.A: Understate the stores balance of the railway
options.B: Inflate the closing stores balance and thereby the Turnover Ratio
options.C: Improve the Turnover Ratio of stores
options.D: Have no effect on the stores balance

e: Outstanding debit balances under Purchase Suspense for bills paid but material not received inflate the closing stores balance, and thereby inflate the Turnover Ratio, distorting the stores position.

q: A stores requirement can be met from a Government department or a public sector undertaking. Obtaining stores from such a source is:

options.A: Not permitted in any circumstances
options.B: A recognised source from which stores may be obtained without inviting tenders
options.C: Permitted only against a Proprietary Article Certificate
options.D: Permitted only through a reverse auction on IREPS

e: Obtaining stores from a Government department or public sector undertaking is a recognised source of supply without inviting tenders, as provided in GFR and Stores Code procurement provisions.

q: The validity of the offers in a stores tender is about to expire and a decision cannot be taken in time. The lowest tenderer agrees to extend the validity of his offer, but only if the rate payable to him is increased. The correct position is that:

options.A: The extension can be accepted at the increased rate, as the tenderer remains the lowest
options.B: Validity can be extended only on the original rates and terms of the offer; a demand for a higher rate amounts to a fresh offer and cannot be accepted as an extension
options.C: The increased rate can be paid after the purchase order is placed, by an amendment
options.D: The earnest money of the tenderer is forfeited for seeking a higher rate

e: Extension of offer validity is valid only on the original rates and terms. A demand for a higher rate for extending validity amounts to a fresh offer and cannot be accepted as an extension.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Splitting a single stores demand into smaller indents merely to bring the purchase within the financial powers of a lower authority is not permissible.
2. On the recommendation of the Tender Committee, an order may be split between the lowest tenderer and another acceptable tenderer who matches the lowest rate, where the quantity required is large or delivery is urgent.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Splitting a demand merely to bring it within lower financial powers is impermissible, while splitting an order between L1 and another tenderer matching the L1 rate on Tender Committee recommendation for large quantity or urgent delivery is permissible. Hence both statements are correct.

q: In a tender for a stores item notified as a safety item, the lowest offer is from a firm which is not an approved source for that item, while a higher offer is from an approved source. The item can be ordered only:

options.A: From the lowest tenderer, price being the sole criterion in a tender
options.B: From the lowest tenderer, after the depot officer certifies the quality of his material
options.C: From a source approved for the safety item, however attractive the lower rate of the unapproved firm may be
options.D: By splitting the order equally between the two firms

e: A safety item can be ordered only from a source approved for that safety item. Price alone cannot justify ordering from an unapproved firm, however low its rate.

q: During the currency of a stores contract, the Railway invokes the option clause for an additional quantity. The supplier agrees to supply the additional quantity but demands a higher rate for it on the ground of a rise in market prices. For the option quantity, the supplier is payable:

options.A: At the higher rate demanded by him
options.B: At the average of the contract rate and the market rate
options.C: At a rate fixed by the consignee depot
options.D: Only at the rate and on the terms and conditions of the original contract, the option being exercisable on those very terms

e: Under the option clause, additional quantity ordered during contract currency is payable only at the original contract rate and on the original terms and conditions; a market rise does not entitle the supplier to a higher rate for the option quantity.

q: A supplier, without obtaining the written consent of the Railway, assigns his stores contract to another firm controlled by him and asks the Railway to deal with that firm for the balance supplies. The correct position is that:

options.A: The assignment is valid, both firms being under the same management
options.B: The assignment binds the Railway once the supplier intimates it in writing
options.C: A stores contract cannot be assigned or sublet without the written consent of the Railway, and an unauthorised assignment may be dealt with under the conditions of contract
options.D: The depot storekeeper may recognise the new firm by changing the name in the receipt note

e: A stores contract cannot be assigned or sublet without written consent of the Railway under the IRS Conditions of Contract. Unauthorised assignment does not bind the Railway and may be dealt with under the contract conditions.

q: A supplier's works are flooded and supplies under a stores contract are delayed. The competent authority, on examining the facts, accepts that the delay was due to an event beyond the supplier's control covered by the force majeure clause of the contract. The delay so occasioned is dealt with by:

options.A: Levying liquidated damages in the ordinary course, force majeure being no defence
options.B: Granting a suitable extension of the delivery period without levy of liquidated damages for the period covered by the accepted force majeure event
options.C: Cancelling the contract and recovering the full contract value from the supplier
options.D: Paying the supplier a higher rate for the delayed supplies as compensation

e: Where delay is accepted as due to a force majeure event beyond the supplier control, a suitable extension of delivery period is granted without liquidated damages for the period covered by that event.

q: A contractor, when called upon to produce his books of account and cost records for examination under the book examination clause of his stores contract, refuses to allow the examination. The refusal amounts to:

options.A: No breach at all, the clause being only directory in nature
options.B: A ground for the depot to stop stock verification of the item
options.C: A matter to be decided by the purchaser of scrap from the depot
options.D: A failure to comply with a condition of the contract, on which the Railway may take action in accordance with the conditions of contract

e: Refusal to produce books and cost records for examination under the book examination clause is failure to comply with a contract condition, on which the Railway may take action in accordance with the conditions of contract.

q: A consignment of stores has arrived at a depot and is lying in the receipt section awaiting inspection, no receipt note having yet been issued for it. During the stock verification of the depot held at that time, the consignment is correctly treated as:

options.A: Not forming part of the priced stock balance, the material being taken into stock only after inspection, acceptance and issue of the receipt note
options.B: An excess of stock, to be recorded on a stock sheet in favour of the stockholder
options.C: Part of the priced stock balance of the item, the material being physically present in the depot
options.D: Scrap, as it has not been entered in the bin card

e: Material awaiting inspection with no receipt note issued is not yet taken into stock and does not form part of the priced stock balance; it enters stock only after inspection, acceptance and issue of the receipt note.

q: Material has just arrived at a depot and its inspection is still pending. A consuming department, citing an urgent requirement, demands that the material be issued to it at once, the inspection to follow later. The correct course is that:

options.A: The material is issued at once, urgency dispensing with inspection
options.B: The material is issued against a verbal order of the depot officer, inspection being a formality
options.C: The supplier is asked to issue the material directly to the department
options.D: Issue from stock can be made only after the material has been inspected, accepted and taken into stock under a receipt note; urgency does not dispense with acceptance into stock

e: Issue can be made only from accepted stock taken in under a receipt note after inspection and acceptance. Urgency does not dispense with inspection and acceptance into stock before issue.

q: In the internal check of a depot's priced accounts, it is found that one and the same receipt of stores has been posted twice in the Priced Stores Ledger, so that both the quantity and the value of the item stand overstated, though the physical stock is correct. The error is rectified by:

options.A: Preparing a stock sheet for a shortage and recovering the value from the stockholder
options.B: Reversing the duplicate posting after linking the entry with the single receipt note supporting the receipt, so that the priced account agrees with the documents and the physical balance
options.C: Altering the bin card quantities to match the doubled ledger balance
options.D: Debiting the doubled value to Purchase Suspense permanently

e: A duplicate posting in the Priced Stores Ledger is rectified by reversing the duplicate entry after linking with the single supporting receipt note, restoring agreement with documents and physical balance, without treating it as a stockholder shortage.

q: While preparing the Stores Budget, the estimates of works and maintenance programmes already contain provision for the stores to be drawn for them, but the deduct entry is omitted from the stores estimates by oversight. Unless corrected, the omission results in:

options.A: Double budgeting of the same requirement, the value of the stores being provided both in the programme estimates and again in the Stores Budget, which is corrected by providing the deduct entry
options.B: The stores balance of the railway being understated
options.C: No error at all, the deduct entry being optional
options.D: The Turnover Ratio of stores being improved

e: Omitting the deduct entry in the Stores Budget when programme estimates already provide for stores to be drawn causes double budgeting of the same requirement; the deduct entry corrects this duplication.

q: Midway through the year, the maintenance and works programmes of the consuming departments of a railway are substantially expanded and the requirements of stores rise correspondingly. The Stores Budget of the railway is dealt with by:

options.A: Leaving it unchanged, a Stores Budget once prepared being incapable of revision
options.B: Revising the anticipated debits and credits of stores in the revised estimates in step with the revised programmes, the Stores Budget being a derived budget
options.C: Meeting the extra requirement entirely from dead surplus, without any budget revision
options.D: Debiting the extra stores directly to the Stock Adjustment Account

e: The Stores Budget is a derived budget. When works and maintenance programmes are expanded mid-year, anticipated debits and credits are revised in the revised estimates in step with the revised programmes.

q: Against a stores bill on which advance payment has been made, the material is received at the destination depot in part only and that part is inspected and accepted. The debit outstanding under Purchase Suspense for the bill is cleared:

options.A: In full, as soon as any part of the material is received
options.B: Only at the close of the financial year, whatever the receipts in between
options.C: By transfer to Sales Suspense for the part received
options.D: To the extent of the value of the material actually received, inspected, accepted and linked with the bill, the balance remaining outstanding until the remaining material is received or the amount is otherwise recovered

e: Advance-paid bills under Purchase Suspense are cleared only to the extent of material actually received, inspected, accepted and linked with the bill; the balance remains outstanding until the remaining material is received or the amount recovered.

q: A purchaser is the highest bidder for two lots of scrap in an e-auction, but he pays the full sale value of only one lot within the time allowed and defaults on the other. Delivery is correctly allowed:

options.A: Of both lots, the purchaser being the highest bidder for both
options.B: Of neither lot, the whole auction being cancelled for all purchasers
options.C: Of the lot for which the full sale value has been paid, the other lot being dealt with as a default under the conditions of sale
options.D: Of the unpaid lot first, so that the depot is cleared quickly

e: Delivery of scrap lots is allowed only for the lot whose full sale value has been paid within the allowed time; the defaulted lot is dealt with as a default under the conditions of sale.

q: Immediately after an e-auction of scrap closes, the highest bidder for a lot informs the depot that he had bid by mistake and asks that his bid be treated as withdrawn. The correct position is that:

options.A: The bid can be withdrawn freely at any time before delivery of the material
options.B: The bid is binding on the bidder under the conditions of sale, and his failure to complete the purchase attracts the consequences provided therein, such as forfeiture of the earnest money and re-auction of the lot
options.C: The lot must be given to him at half the bid price as a compromise
options.D: The earnest money of all bidders for the lot is forfeited to the Railway

e: A bid in an e-auction is binding under the conditions of sale. Failure to complete the purchase attracts consequences such as forfeiture of earnest money and re-auction of the lot; it cannot be freely withdrawn after closure.

q: An item declared surplus in a depot is required by another depot, but the cost of transporting it to that depot would exceed the useful value of the item itself. In such a case, the competent authority may properly decide to:

options.A: Transfer the item in every case, transport cost being irrelevant
options.B: Destroy the item at the holding depot without any sanction
options.C: Retain the item in stock indefinitely until transport becomes cheaper
options.D: Dispose of the item locally in accordance with the rules, instead of effecting an uneconomical transfer, economy and financial propriety governing the choice between transfer and disposal

e: Where transport cost to a requiring depot would exceed the useful value of a surplus item, the competent authority may dispose of it locally under the rules instead of effecting an uneconomical transfer, economy governing the choice.

q: An XYZ review of the stores of a depot brings out an item of which only a small quantity is held, but the value of the stock held of that item is the highest in the depot. The control measure principally called for in respect of such an item is:

options.A: Loose control, the quantity held being small
options.B: Close watch and control over the stock held and its replenishment, the classification being based on the value of the inventory held of the item
options.C: Immediate declaration of the item as dead surplus
options.D: Transfer of the item to the Tools and Plant register

e: XYZ analysis classifies by value of inventory held. An item with small quantity but highest stock value calls for close watch and control over stock and replenishment, not loose control.

q: An item is classified as scarce in SDE analysis, its procurement being difficult and time-consuming. The stocking and procurement of such an item are correctly arranged by:

options.A: Initiating procurement well in advance and keeping adequate coverage under close watch, so that the long and uncertain procurement does not cause a stock-out
options.B: Ordering the item only after the stock is completely exhausted
options.C: Procuring the item through petty local purchases as and when required
options.D: Holding no stock of the item at any time

e: A scarce item in SDE analysis, difficult and time-consuming to procure, requires procurement initiated well in advance with adequate coverage under close watch, to avoid stock-out from long uncertain lead time.

q:
Consider the following statements about the service level of a stock item:
1. Raising the service level of an item requires a higher safety stock to be held for it, which increases the inventory carrying cost borne on that item.
2. A lower safety stock reduces the carrying cost but exposes the depot to a greater risk of stock-out of the item.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Raising service level needs higher safety stock and increases carrying cost, while lower safety stock reduces carrying cost but increases stock-out risk. Hence both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about shortages of stores such as coal and oils, which are subject to normal losses in handling and transit:
1. A shortage which is within the prescribed permissible limit for such stores is adjusted by write-off under the sanction of the competent authority.
2. A shortage which exceeds the permissible limit is enquired into and the responsibility for the excess loss is fixed before it is adjusted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Shortages of coal, oils and similar stores within the prescribed permissible limit for handling and transit losses are written off under competent sanction, while excess beyond the limit is enquired into and responsibility fixed before adjustment. Hence both statements are correct.

q: For an import of stores against a Letter of Credit, the supplier presents shipping documents which do not conform to the documents stipulated in the credit, though he states that the goods have actually been shipped. Payment under the credit is correctly made:

options.A: Only against presentation of the stipulated documents conforming to the terms of the credit, a discrepancy in the documents being first rectified or dealt with in accordance with those terms
options.B: In cash to the supplier's agent at the Indian port
options.C: At once, the physical shipment of the goods being sufficient for payment
options.D: By the consignee depot out of its imprest cash

e: Payment under a Letter of Credit is made only against stipulated documents conforming to the credit terms. A discrepancy must first be rectified or dealt with under those terms; mere shipment of goods is not sufficient.

q: A consignment of imported stores has reached the Indian port, but customs clearance of the consignment is still pending. An inland depot which is the ultimate consignee of the stores can take the consignment into its priced stock:

options.A: From the date the vessel reaches the Indian port
options.B: As soon as the foreign supplier intimates despatch of the consignment
options.C: From the date the Letter of Credit is opened in favour of the supplier
options.D: Only after the consignment has been cleared through Customs on payment of the duty payable and has thereafter been received, inspected and accepted at the depot

e: An inland depot can take imported stores into priced stock only after customs clearance on payment of duty and thereafter receipt, inspection and acceptance at the depot, not from vessel arrival, despatch intimation or opening of the credit.

q: A tenderer in a stores tender furnishes his Earnest Money Deposit by a personal cheque of the proprietor of his firm, though the tender conditions prescribe only specified forms such as cash, demand draft, bank guarantee or fixed deposit receipt. His offer is liable to be:

options.A: Treated as not conforming to the tender conditions in respect of the deposit, and dealt with as a non-responsive offer in accordance with those conditions
options.B: Accepted, the form of the deposit being immaterial
options.C: Accepted after a fine is recovered from the tenderer
options.D: Considered after the price packet of every other tenderer is opened

e: Earnest Money Deposit furnished in a form not prescribed in the tender conditions, such as a personal cheque where only cash, demand draft, bank guarantee or fixed deposit receipt are prescribed, makes the offer non-conforming and liable to be treated as non-responsive.

q: A firm is registered with the Railways for the supply of items of one trade group. It submits an offer in a limited tender invited for an item of a different trade group, for which it is neither registered nor assessed. The correct treatment of the offer is that:

options.A: Registration for any one group entitles the firm to supply every stores item
options.B: The offer establishes the firm's registration for the new group automatically
options.C: The depot officer may treat the firm as registered for the new group on the strength of the offer
options.D: Registration being granted for specific items or groups after assessment of the firm, the firm is not eligible for the item of the other group unless it is registered or otherwise approved for that group or item

e: Registration is granted for specific items or groups after assessment. A firm registered for one trade group is not eligible for an item of another group unless registered or otherwise approved for that group or item.

q: A member of a Stores Tender Committee finds that one of the tenderers under consideration is a firm in which he has a personal interest. The proper course for the member is to:

options.A: Participate in the deliberations and recommend that firm, disclosing nothing
options.B: Decide the tender single-handed in favour of that firm
options.C: Declare his interest in the matter and keep out of the evaluation and deliberations relating to that tender
options.D: Resign from the Tender Committee permanently for all tenders

e: A Tender Committee member with a personal interest in a tenderer must declare his interest and keep out of evaluation and deliberations for that tender, to preserve impartiality and avoid conflict of interest.
